cards.text: Later, there's a new king on the throne: King Belshazzar. He throws a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and he drinks wine with them. A THOUSAND guests, friend, and I can't fit a dozen cookies on one tray without one sliding off.
Under the influence of the wine, Belshazzar gives an order. He wants the gold and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken brought in.

cards.question: Belshazzar wants the gold and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar took. Where did Nebuchadnezzar take them from?
Belshazzar has the temple vessels brought in so they can be sent back to Jerusalem.

cards.text: So in come the gold vessels from the house of God, and the king drinks from them with his nobles, his wives and his concubines. Cups from God's own house, friend, passed around like it's the office holiday party.

cards.question: While Belshazzar's guests drink wine from the vessels of God's house, who do they praise?

answers.text: Their gods of gold and silver

cards.text: At that moment, the fingers of a human hand appear and write on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. Just fingers and a wall, friend, and NOBODY sent that an invitation.

cards.question: At Belshazzar's feast, the king sees the hand while it is still writing on the wall.

cards.text: Belshazzar's face goes pale, his hips give way, and his knees knock together. Knees knocking in front of a thousand nobles, friend, and I'd be knocking too, and I don't even HAVE knees.

cards.question: Shaking, Belshazzar calls out for help with the writing on the wall. Who does he call for?

cards.text: He offers whoever reads the writing and explains it purple clothes, a gold chain around the neck and the spot of third highest ruler in the kingdom. Friend, that's a PROMOTION for reading one wall.

cards.question: Belshazzar's wise men can read the writing on the wall, but they can't tell him what it means.

cards.text: Now Belshazzar is even more terrified, his face even paler, and his nobles are bewildered. Pale on top of pale, friend, the man is the color of raw cookie dough.
Then the queen hears the outcry and walks into the banquet hall. She says, “O king, may you live forever!” and tells him, “Do not let your thoughts terrify you, or your face grow pale.”

cards.question: The queen tells Belshazzar there's a man in his kingdom with the spirit of the holy gods in him. Which king made that man chief of the magicians?
The queen tells Belshazzar to summon ___, and he will give him the interpretation.

cards.text: So Daniel is brought before the king. Belshazzar asks him, “Are you Daniel, one of the exiles my father the king brought from Judah?”

He says he's heard Daniel has extraordinary wisdom, and his own wise men couldn't read the writing. Then he makes Daniel the same offer: purple clothes, a gold chain and third highest ruler in the kingdom.

cards.question: Purple clothes, a gold chain and a big promotion. What does Daniel tell Belshazzar about his gifts?
Since Daniel turns down Belshazzar's gifts, he also refuses to read the writing on the wall.

cards.text: Before Daniel reads a word, he tells the king about his father: the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar sovereignty and greatness, glory and honor. The king asked for a reading, friend, and he's getting a family history.

cards.question: Daniel says Nebuchadnezzar's heart became arrogant and his spirit was hardened with pride. What happened to Nebuchadnezzar then?

answers.text: He was deposed from his throne
He built a new royal palace

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar was driven away from mankind, his mind like that of a beast, and he ate grass like an ox. That lasted until he acknowledged that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of mankind.

cards.question: Daniel says Belshazzar never knew what happened to his father Nebuchadnezzar.

cards.text: Daniel says Belshazzar exalted himself against the Lord of heaven. He drank from the vessels of God's house and praised gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone, “which cannot see or hear or understand.”

cards.question: What does Daniel say Belshazzar has failed to do?

answers.text: Glorify the God who holds his breath in His hand
Send the exiles back home to Judah
Rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem

cards.question: Daniel says the hand that wrote on the wall was sent by the gods Belshazzar praised.

cards.text: Then Daniel reads the inscription: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN. Four words, friend, and I bet you could hear a sprinkle drop in that hall.

cards.question: MENE is the first word on Belshazzar's wall. What does Daniel say it means?

answers.text: God has numbered the days of his reign
God has forgiven the pride of the king
God will add more years to his reign

cards.question: Daniel says TEKEL means Belshazzar has been weighed on the scales and found ___.
Daniel says PERES means Belshazzar's kingdom has been divided and given over to the ___ and ___.
After hearing all that, Belshazzar still has Daniel clothed in purple and proclaimed third highest ruler in the kingdom.

cards.text: That very night, Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans is slain. The party is over, friend, and so is his reign.

cards.question: Belshazzar is slain that very night. Who receives his kingdom?

cards.text: Darius the Mede receives the kingdom at the age of sixty-two. Four words on a wall, friend, and every one of them meant business.

findings.problem: The question types follow a pattern. Stop 1 goes MC, TF, MC, TF, MC, TF, MC, then FB. Stop 2 opens with the same strict MC, TF alternation for its first seven choice cards (cards 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13), so it repeats stop 1's pattern. Stop 1 also has only one fill in the blank.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Daniel 5:19 is never covered. Card 5 cites 5:18 and card 6 jumps to 5:20, so the baker never hears that every nation trembled before Nebuchadnezzar and that he killed, spared, exalted and humbled whomever he wished. This is part of Daniel's speech, and it sets up the fall in 5:20.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Give them to my people" is close to what Daniel actually says in 5:17: "give your rewards to someone else." A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Glorify the God who holds his breath in His hand," reads like the idiom "holding one's breath." The text says God "holds in His hand your very breath and all your ways." The answer is also noticeably longer than the two wrong answers.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Most of stop 2's story cards are plain retellings with no Papa Dorin voice. Cards 1, 2, 7 and 9 carry Daniel's whole speech this way. Stop 2 has only three voiced lines (cards 5, 12 and 17), so this stretch reads stripped down.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
